verdict.rationale: CloudConvert's own docs say API keys can be created with selectable scopes that limit access, and OAuth 2.0 flows can issue access tokens on behalf of users. That is a direct least-privilege credential mechanism suited to agents, but the evidence is a single thin sentence with no detail on what the scopes cover. missing for 10: documented list and granularity of scopes, key expiry/rotation and revocation details, per-agent or multiple-key management, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: When creating an API key, you can select scopes to limit access.
CloudConvert supports OAuth 2.0's authorization code grant flow and implicit grant flow to issue access tokens on behalf of users.
